title: Hot-prefix canonicalization and stable-ttl anchoring for embedding cache
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Problem: Reranking endpoints observe tail latency and wasted compute due to near-duplicate embedding requests and inconsistent prefix forms (whitespace, punctuation variants, HTML snippets) resulting in cache fragmentation. Existing prefix caching reduces some duplication but is brittle for noisy user text and tenant-namespace skew. Goal: introduce a canonicalization + anchored-ttl scheme for hot prefixes and a stable content-hash key derivation to reduce duplicate embedding calls while preserving deterministic invalidation semantics and multi-tenant isolation. This ticket designs the algorithm, implements the service-side canonicalizer and key layer, and evaluates quality and latency tradeoffs on production-like traffic.
acceptance_criteria: 95% reduction in identical-key embedding calls for hot prefixes during test workload compared to baseline (measured over 24h replay)
End-to-end median latency for small rerank requests improves by >= 15% with no regression in 99th percentile beyond allocated SLO
No cross-tenant cache leakage: keys include tenant salt and pass unit tests covering tenant isolation
Cache invalidation semantics preserved: model version rollout and canonicalization changes trigger deterministic tombstone entries and do not silently serve stale vectors
Instrumentation and dashboards added: duplicate-hit rate, canonicalization transforms distribution, TTL-anchor churn, and false-positive dedupe incidents
design_decisions: Apply a two-stage key derivation: (1) normalizing canonicalizer that strips HTML, collapses whitespace, lowercases, and applies language-aware token trimming for very long inputs; (2) content-hash using BLAKE3 keyed with tenant_id for deterministic namespacing

Hot-prefix anchoring: for inputs that share a short prefix (first 64 bytes normalized) we store a small prefix index mapping to canonical keys to accelerate lookups without materializing all permutations

Stable TTL anchoring: instead of assigning TTLs at insertion only, attach a lightweight tombstone epoch tag derived from model_version and canonicalizer_schema_version; eviction honors tombstone epoch to prevent stale serving across rollouts
Bloom prefilter at the gateway layer to avoid unnecessary datastore lookups for obviously unseen keys, tuned to low false-positive target (0.5%) to minimize extra embedding generation
No on-the-fly approximate nearest neighbor dedupe in cache: we keep exactness for reranking correctness and only dedupe exact (canonicalized+hashed) matches to avoid ranking regressions
Graceful degradation: if canonicalizer fails (bad unicode, OOM), fallback to fallback-normalization with a conservative hash and mark metric so we can triage
tradeoffs: Aggressive canonicalization increases dedupe but risks collapsing semantically distinct inputs (e.g., punctuation that changes meaning). We mitigate via schema_versioning and conservative heuristics
Bloom filter reduces datastore IOPS but introduces small FP rate which may cause missed cache hits to be treated as misses; chosen FP target balances CPU vs extra embed cost
Anchored TTL requires slightly more metadata per entry (epoch tag) increasing storage by ~4-8 bytes per key, acceptable for hot-path savings
Tenant-keyed hashing prevents cross-tenant dedupe savings but is necessary for isolation and compliance
Runtime canonicalization adds CPU at request path; we offload heavy normalization to a lightweight fast-path and allow async re-canonicalization in background for cold keys
rollout_plan: 1) Implement canonicalizer library and unit tests behind config flag (dev env)
2) Add key-derivation to staging cache layer, enable Bloom prefiltering and metrics, run 48h replay of production traffic to quantify improvement
3) Canary deploy to 10% of traffic with read-only cache injection (observe dedupe but not serve from cache) to validate safety
4) Enable write-through for canary if canary metrics pass (dedupe_rate, latency, false_positive_alerts) for 72h
5) Gradual rollout in 10% increments with automated rollback on error budget or false-positive spikes
6) After stable rollout, enable aggressive canonicalizer schema on a separate flag and stage similarly
7) Post-rollout: run a 7-day regression eval using eval prompts and reranking quality checks to ensure no ranking degradations
monitoring_and_metrics: false_positive_dedupe_incidents (cases where dedupe served incorrectly flagged via A/B checks)
comments: 2025-02-05 - Devin Cho: Spike complete. Prototype canonicalizer reduced duplicate keys by ~60% on a 6-hour replay using conservative rules. Bloom filter tuned to 0.6% FP showed ~12% datastore IOPS reduction.

2025-02-12 - Sofia Martinez: Design review notes - PM requested tenant salt to be explicit in keys and audit log for cache hits added. Research asked for sample-level QA harness to detect semantically collapsing cases.

2025-02-20 - Devin Cho: Implemented tombstone epoch tagging and added unit tests for model_version change invalidation. Local perf shows +3% CPU on gateway but 18% lower token-generation calls for rerank microbenchmarks.

2025-03-02 - QA (Arjun Patel): Staging replay (48h) passed stability checks. One incident: canonicalizer normalized 'C++' to 'c' in corner case; added exception rule to preserve short code tokens. Patch merged to PR 3012.
2025-03-04 - PM (Leah Kim): Approved canary. Business metrics owner confirmed acceptable risk window for canary writes. Scheduled canary for 2025-03-06 10:00 UTC.
notes: Follow-up: evaluate integrating approximate semantic dedupe layer that operates offline to fuse highly similar vectors for long-tail cost savings
Add a lightweight per-tenant 'canonicalizer profile' configurable via Console so enterprise customers can opt into stricter or looser canonicalization
